projects.title: OpsRadar
projects.description: A lightweight alert bridge for Windows and Linux hosts where a full observability stack is too much.
projects.story: OpsRadar brings host alerts and heartbeats into one self-hosted web console. Thin Node.js CLI agents report to an Express API, while a React admin interface provides inventory management, scoped alerts, and in-app notifications. The project is being presented under its new name, OpsRadar; the reference implementation was named LongShot / AlertOn.
projects.imageAlt: Conceptual illustration of host agents sending orange heartbeat signals to a central alert console and database
features: Alert ingest, resolution, and heartbeats from Node-only agents on Windows or Linux.
Per-server API keys for agents, JWT sign-in for the web console, and optional authenticator-based TOTP.
Inventory organized by country, application, group, and server, with scoped user visibility.
Configurable alert retention and heartbeat-based detection of unavailable hosts.
Docker Compose control plane with PostgreSQL persistence; systemd and Windows service setup for agents.

projects.title: Roach
projects.description: A shop inventory application that connects product records, QR scanning, stock movements, and checkout.
projects.story: Roach gives each shop a private workspace for its products, stock movements, invoices, and alerts. A React front end is served through Nginx, which forwards API and image requests to Express. MongoDB stores the inventory and sales records, while Docker Compose brings the services together.
projects.imageAlt: Conceptual illustration of product shelves, a scanner, an inventory panel, and a checkout receipt
features: Product records with photos or camera stills, prices, costs, quantities, and reorder levels.
Downloadable product QR labels, camera scanning, and name or SKU search as a fallback.
Restocking, multi-item checkout, stock movement history, and invoices with sale-time line snapshots.
Sales reports for units, revenue, cost, and profit, plus low-stock and out-of-stock notifications.
Shop-scoped accounts, a 30-day trial, and operator-recorded offline payments that extend access without deleting data.

opsradar.subtitle: A small signal path. A clearer operational picture.
opsradar.challenge: Legacy and resource-constrained hosts still need a way to report failures. A lightweight agent can send actionable alerts without installing a metrics database or a full observability stack on each machine.
opsradar.flow: Agents send alerts, resolutions, and heartbeats to the API. The API persists records in PostgreSQL. The React console reads scoped data through the API; it does not connect to the database directly.
takeaways: Keep the agent Node-only and move persistence and administration to the control plane. This keeps deployment practical on constrained hosts.
Per-server ingest keys and web JWT sessions serve different callers. Keeping those paths distinct makes access easier to reason about.
Heartbeat timing and retention are operational choices. A missing heartbeat is a host-liveness signal, not a complete diagnosis of the application.
opsradar.scope: Alerts and host liveness are the focus. Time-series metrics, log indexing, and distributed tracing are outside this implementation.

roach.subtitle: From a product on a shelf to a recorded sale.
roach.challenge: A shop needs a consistent record of what is on hand, what moved, and what sold. Roach connects product identification with stock changes and invoices while keeping each shop’s records separate.
roach.flow: The browser reaches Nginx, which serves the React app and forwards API and image requests to Express. Express checks access and ownership before reading or changing MongoDB records. Images live in upload storage or optional Cloudinary.
takeaways: Restock, adjustment, and checkout movements create a history behind the current quantity rather than leaving only an unexplained number.
Invoice lines retain the name, SKU, prices, and cost at checkout time, so later product edits do not redefine a past sale.
A product QR code identifies an item. Ownership and account-access checks still belong at the API boundary.
roach.scope: Payment extensions are recorded offline by an operator. There is no card-payment gateway. Email features require SMTP configuration.

opsradar.name: Alert lifecycle
opsradar.title: From host signal to an actionable alert.
steps: An engineer or host process reports an operational issue.
The agent submits the alert with its per-server API key.
The API stores the record and the console presents scoped alerts.
A resolution updates the alert lifecycle.

opsradar.name: Host liveness
opsradar.title: Know when a host stops checking in.
steps: A Node agent runs on Windows or Linux.
Periodic heartbeats reach the control plane.
The service checks the elapsed time since the last beat.
The console exposes host availability to operators.

opsradar.name: Operator workflow
opsradar.title: Give operational signals the right context.
steps: Arrange inventory by country, application, group, and server.
User access determines which alerts are visible.
Use the alert inbox and notification feed.
Apply configured retention to stored alerts.
